config.video_time: Simulation steps only; API waits omitted

protocol_notes: 26 recorded Jev episodes, including failed prompt-development attempts. Counts across settings are descriptive, not statistical success rates.
The model receives structured telemetry and explicit control guidance, not gameplay images. CarRacing includes future centerline waypoints; Walker additionally includes torso position.
NumericJev alone decodes each action component on [-1,1). The final grid lower endpoint is executed. Python does not replace Jev decisions with a fallback controller.
All components share one request per tree level. K=10 / 0.005 uses three sequential requests per action; the other tested settings use two.
Simulation pauses for API calls. Videos omit those waits; they do not demonstrate real-time control. Mean action latency includes all sequential tree calls but excludes rendering/physics.
Box2D games integrate at 50 Hz. CarRacing holds actions for 10 frames; Lander/Walker for 5. MountainCar holds 4 discrete steps and displays seconds at its 30-fps rendering rate.

GIFs are unaccelerated short excerpts; the full-video tab shows the entire recorded episode. Per-run archives contain full requests/responses, executed actions, rules or source snapshots, and original summaries.
K/precision comparison uses one fixed track seed, option order, and prompt per setting. It supports a local comparison, not a general claim that more precision helps or larger K hurts.
